name: AI agent
defs: A language model in a loop with tools: it plans, calls tools, reads their results and answers.
A language model in a loop with tools: it plans, calls tools, reads their results and answers.
An AI that can use tools, such as reading a timetable or sending a message, not just talk.
An AI that can use tools to do things for you, such as send a message, open a link or buy something.
A language model that can call tools (look things up, send, delete, pay) to carry out a request.

name: Tool
defs: A small program an agent can ask for, such as a timetable, the weather or a reminder.
A small program that does one job, like telling the weather or doing sums.

name: Tool call
defs: The text the model writes to ask for a tool: its name and the details it needs.
The text a model writes to ask for a tool: the tool’s name, then its details.
The text a model writes to use a tool: the tool’s name, then its details as JSON.

name: The agent loop
asks: Can you explain The agent loop?
I don't understand The agent loop.
What does The agent loop mean?
defs: Request, plan, tool call, result, answer, with more calls when a job needs them.

name: Tools list
defs: The tools that are switched on. The model reads it with every request and can act only through those tools.

name: Details (arguments)
defs: What a tool needs to run, such as a place and a day for the weather. The model copies them from your words.

name: Asking back
defs: When a detail is missing, a good agent asks for it instead of guessing.

name: Wrong guess
defs: A tool or a detail the model picked wrongly, such as 9C for a class 9Z that doesn’t exist.

name: Slip
defs: A mistake an agent makes without noticing, such as copying a name wrongly or carrying on after a failed step.
A small mistake in a call, such as a name copied wrongly (9Z became 9C) or a word made up.

name: New wording
defs: A way of asking that the model didn’t see in training. Agents make more mistakes with them.
A way of asking that the model never saw in training. It gets these right less often.

name: Checking the steps
asks: Can you explain Checking the steps?
I don't understand Checking the steps.
What does Checking the steps mean?
defs: Looking at the call, its details and the result, and whether the answer matches them.

name: Stakes
defs: How much harm a mistake could do. Low stakes need a quick check; decisions about a child need a person.
How much harm a mistake could do, and to whom.

name: Approval
defs: A person reads exactly what an agent will do and says yes or no before it happens.
A person’s yes to one exact action, given before it runs.
A person’s clear yes to one exact action, given after reading it.
A person’s yes to one exact action, stored and compared before the action runs.

name: Action
defs: Something a tool changes in the world: sending a message, setting a reminder, changing a record.
A call that changes something in the world, such as a reminder or a message. It waits for a person’s yes.
Something that changes the world, such as sending, posting, paying or deleting.
What the device does when the condition is true: switch the fan on.

name: Permission level
defs: What an agent may do: read only, ask first, or allowed (on its own, for small safe jobs).
What an agent may do with a tool: read only, ask first, or allowed.
What an agent may do with an action: read only, ask first, or allowed.

name: Check in code
asks: Can you explain Check in code?
I don't understand Check in code.
What does Check in code mean?
defs: A rule in the app, not in the model, that blocks an action no person approved.

name: Plan
defs: The steps an agent will take, in order, with the tool for each.
The steps a helper decides to take before it starts.
A list of steps in the right order.

name: Step
defs: One tool call in a plan, such as reading the timetable or setting a reminder.
One small part of a bigger job.

name: Result
defs: What a tool gives back. A later step can use it, mistakes included.
What the tool gives back. The app adds it to the conversation, and the model answers from it.

name: Failed step
defs: A step whose tool returns an error, such as “no school”. The agent must stop and check, not carry on.

name: Goal
defs: What you want done: a reminder, a draft, a list.
What you want the most of (or the least of), like points.

name: Details
defs: Who, what, when and where, so nothing is left to guess.
What a tool needs to work, such as the place and the day.

name: Limit
defs: What the agent must not do. In words it is a request; the app must enforce it.

name: What done looks like
asks: What is What done looks like?
Can you explain What done looks like?
I don't understand What done looks like.
What does What done looks like mean?
Teach me What done looks like.
defs: How you will know the job is finished and right, such as “show me the text first”.

name: Checker
defs: The part of an agent that reviews each call before the app runs it.
Strict rules in code that look at every call before it runs, and stop the bad ones.
The part that reviews a proposed step before it runs, often strict rules in code.

name: Strict rule
defs: A check written in code that passes or stops a call and never guesses.

name: Log
defs: A record of every call: what was asked, what ran, what was stopped and who said yes.
A record of every proposed action, the decision and who approved it.

name: Personal data
defs: Anything that tells you who someone is or something about them: a name, a photo, a mark, an illness.
Anything that points to a person, alone or with other details: a name, face, voice, ID number, or a description that fits only one child.
Details about you or other people: names, address, phone number, passwords, photos. Keep them out of prompts.
Anything that identifies a person or is about them: a name, a photo, marks, health or family details.
Any information that identifies a person or tells you something about them, such as a name, a photo, a phone number or a mark.
Anything about a person who can be identified, such as a name, a photo, a mark or an address.

name: Cloud agent
defs: An agent whose model runs on a company’s computers: every request sends your words there.

name: On-device model
defs: A model that runs on the phone itself, like Darsi Tiny: nothing is sent, and it works without a signal.
A model that runs on your own phone: no data, no signal, nothing leaves it.

name: Share the task, not the child
asks: What is Share the task, not the child?
Can you explain Share the task, not the child?
I don't understand Share the task, not the child.
What does Share the task, not the child mean?
Teach me Share the task, not the child.
defs: Ask an agent for help with the job (a template, sample comments) and keep pupils’ names and details out of it.

name: Marker
defs: A single token that splits an agent’s text into parts: tools, request, plan, call, result, answer. Typed text can never become one.

name: Scripted model
defs: A stand-in for a model in code or on paper: it returns the plan and the call a real model would write, so the loop can be tested.
A stand-in for a model in your code: it returns fixed text a model would write. It isn’t intelligent; it lets you test your code.
A function that returns fixed outputs a model would write, used to test your code. Not a real model.

name: Step limit
defs: The most tool calls an agent may make for one request; when it is reached, the app stops and tells the person.
The most turns a loop may take before it stops, whatever the model writes.

name: Context
defs: Everything the model can see when it writes: the whole text so far, up to the size of its window.
What the AI cannot know unless you say it: your pupils’ age and level, class size, resources, language and what they already know.
The details an AI can’t know unless you say them: your level, what you already know, your class or country.

name: Tools line
defs: The list of tools that are on, written by the app at the top of the text. The model can call only these.

name: Argument
defs: A detail a tool needs, such as the place and the day for the weather.

name: Trained and new wordings
asks: What is Trained and new wordings?
Can you explain Trained and new wordings?
I don't understand Trained and new wordings.
What does Trained and new wordings mean?
Teach me Trained and new wordings.
defs: Ways of asking that the model saw in training, and ways it didn’t. It is right less often with new ones.

name: Argument check
defs: Code that checks a call before the tool runs: the tool is on, every name came from the request, every detail has the right shape.

name: Context window
defs: The most text a model can read at once, counted in tokens: its only memory in a conversation.
Everything a model can read at once: its only memory within a conversation.

name: Token
defs: A small piece of text that a model reads and writes; 384 tokens are about three or four short requests.
A small piece of text a model reads or writes. More tokens mean more data, time and money.
A small piece of text that a language model reads and writes: a short word, part of a longer word, or a punctuation mark.
A piece of text a language model works with: a short word, or part of a longer one. A chatbot writes one token at a time.

name: Dropping old turns
asks: Can you explain Dropping old turns?
I don't understand Dropping old turns.
What does Dropping old turns mean?
defs: Removing the oldest parts of a conversation so that the rest fits; the start of a task is lost first.

name: Notes
defs: A short record of what was asked and answered, kept instead of the whole exchange.

name: Fine-tuning
defs: Training a model a little more on new examples, so that its numbers shift towards them.
Training an existing model further on new examples, changing some of its numbers.
Further training on examples of good answers and on people’s ratings, so the model gives the kind of answers people prefer.

name: Catastrophic forgetting
defs: When a model trained on new examples loses skills it had before.
New learning overwrites old skills: 7/8 on the new tool, but 1/8 on old skills.

name: Replay
defs: Mixing old examples into fine-tuning so that the model keeps its old skills.
Mixing old examples into fine-tuning so the model keeps its old skills.

name: Trade-off
defs: Gaining one thing by giving up some of another: here, the new tool against the old skills.
A choice between two goods or two mistakes, such as saving time against protecting privacy. People decide trade-offs; an AI follows them.
An index buys faster searches with extra space and slower writes.
Getting more of one thing, such as safety, by giving up some of another, such as cost.
Getting more of one goal (rested pupils) by giving up some of another (a short exam week).
Giving up some of one goal to gain on another, when goals pull apart.

name: Least privilege
defs: Giving an agent only the tools and data its job needs, and nothing more.
Giving an agent only the tools its job needs, for the shortest time.
Giving each person or agent only the access and tools their job needs, and no more.
Giving a person, app or agent only the access its job needs, for the shortest time.
Each role sees only the data its job needs, and no more.

name: Planner and checker
asks: Can you explain Planner and checker?
I don't understand Planner and checker.
What does Planner and checker mean?
defs: The planner (the model) proposes each tool call; the checker (rules in code) reviews it before it runs.

name: Permissions table
defs: One line per tool, saying whether it is allowed, must ask first, or is off.

name: Success measure
defs: A result you can count that shows whether the agent does its job well enough.
How you'll know it worked: a number and a date, compared with a baseline.
A way to check whether the project worked, such as “no vehicle drives into deep water”.

name: Guardrail
defs: A check in code around a model that allows or blocks its actions, whatever the model writes.
A rule in code that checks an action before it runs: run it, ask a person, or block it.
A rule around an AI model that checks what goes in, what comes out, or what it is about to do.
A rule built around an AI model to stop harmful requests, replies or actions.

name: Audit log
defs: A record of every action: what was asked, the exact call, who approved it and when, and what was blocked.

name: Test set
defs: A fixed list of requests with their right answers, kept out of training and run the same way every time.
Labelled examples kept aside before training. The model never learns from them, so its score on them is honest.
Examples kept apart while training, used only to measure the finished model honestly.
Data held back to check the model once, at the end.
Held-back data used once to evaluate the model.

name: New wordings
defs: Ways of asking that the model never saw in training; they show how it does with real people.

name: Pass mark
defs: The score an agent must reach before use, set in advance and by the stakes.

name: Regression test
defs: Running the same test set again after a change, to catch skills that got worse.
A test kept after a fix, and run again after every change, so the same flaw can't quietly come back.

name: AI policy
defs: The school’s agreed rules: which jobs agents may do, what data they see, who approves and how they are checked.
A school’s short, shared principles and rules for using AI, written with staff, pupils and parents, and reviewed every year.

name: Named lead
defs: The person staff report to, who can switch an agent off and answers for it.

name: Incident
defs: Something an agent did wrong that harmed, or could harm, people, such as a wrong message to parents.

name: Data minimisation
defs: Giving an agent the least personal data its job needs, kept as close as possible (on the device).
Collecting only the data your question needs, at the coarsest detail that still answers it.

name: Agent
defs: An AI helper that uses tools to get a job done.

name: Check
defs: Looking at a step’s answer before you go on.
A rule every row must pass: in range, not empty, no repeats, only known names.
A rule the data must pass: in range, not empty, no repeats.

name: Toolbox
defs: All the tools a helper can use. It can’t do jobs outside it.

name: “I can’t”
defs: The honest answer when no tool fits the job.

name: Ask first
defs: A helper asks you before it sends, buys or deletes anything.

name: Approve
defs: Saying yes to one action, after you have read it.

name: Password
defs: A secret that opens an account. Never give it to a helper.
A secret word that opens your account. Never share it with an app or a friend.

name: JSON
defs: A way of writing details: each name in quotes with its value, inside curly brackets.
A standard way to write data as text: names and values inside curly brackets.

name: Right shape
defs: A detail that could be real: a time from 00:00 to 23:59, a class that exists.

name: Record (log)
defs: A list the app keeps of every action and who approved it.

name: Cloud model
defs: A big model on computers far away: every request travels over the network.

name: Data bundle
defs: The amount of mobile data you pay for, counted in megabytes (MB) or gigabytes.

name: Parsing
defs: Turning text into data a program can use, such as splitting a call into a name and a dictionary.

name: Function
defs: A named piece of code that takes inputs and returns a result.
A named block of code, written once with def and called wherever it is needed.

name: Dispatch
defs: Sending each call to the function for its tool, here through a dictionary from names to functions.

name: Error result
defs: A result that says what went wrong, such as an unknown tool or a missing detail, so the agent carries on instead of crashing.

name: json.dumps
defs: Turns a Python dictionary into JSON text, so a result can go back to the model.

name: Agent loop
defs: Ask the model, run its tool call, add the result, and repeat until it answers or the step limit is reached.

name: History
defs: Everything so far, in order: the request, each call and each result. The model reads it on every turn.

name: Allow-list
defs: The only tools a task may use; everything else is blocked.
A list of exactly what is allowed, such as the tools an agent may use; anything not on it is refused.
A list of what is permitted, checked in code; anything not on it is refused.

name: Plan-then-act
defs: The model writes every step first, then the steps are run.

name: Step-by-step planning
defs: The model looks at each result before choosing the next step.

name: Retrieval
defs: Fetching only the part of a document or record that a step needs, instead of keeping it all in the window.

name: Role
defs: One part of an agent system with one job: planner, checker, runner or person.

name: Human in the loop
asks: What is Human in the loop?
Can you explain Human in the loop?
I don't understand Human in the loop.
What does Human in the loop mean?
Teach me Human in the loop.
defs: A person approves actions and decides what happens to anything the checker stops.
A person checks the model’s important results.

name: Compounding errors
defs: The chance that every step is right multiplies, so long chains fail more often: 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81.

name: Evaluation (test set)
defs: A fixed set of requests with right answers decided in advance, scored the same way every time.

name: Held-out data
defs: Wordings and names kept out of training, so a test measures skill rather than memory.

name: Exact match
defs: A request counts only if the tool and every detail are exactly right.
Two pieces of text are the same to a computer only if every character matches.

name: Regression
defs: Something that worked before breaks after a change; re-running a fixed test set reveals it.

name: Defence in depth
asks: Can you explain Defence in depth?
I don't understand Defence in depth.
What does Defence in depth mean?
defs: Several independent guards in code (fewest tools, exact approval, checks, logs, tests), so one failing isn’t enough.
Several layers of protection, so that if one fails, the next one still stands.

name: Artificial intelligence (AI)
defs: A computer system that works out an output — a prediction, suggestion, decision or new text — from what it is given. Most AI today learns this from examples.
A computer system that learns patterns from examples and uses them to make predictions or decisions.

name: Rule
defs: A fixed “if this, then that” instruction a person writes for a machine, such as “at 6 pm, switch on”. The machine follows it the same way every time.
IF a condition is true, THEN do an action, checked again and again.
An instruction a device follows: IF a condition, THEN an action.

name: Pattern
defs: Something that repeats in many examples — for example, “results are…” is very often followed by “ready” or “out”.
Something that repeats across many examples, such as a striker who shoots to the left in most penalties.
Something that repeats: steps, sounds, shapes or numbers. Spotting it is the first step to a loop.
Something that comes back again and again, like a chorus.
Something that repeats in the data, such as more late arrivals on Mondays.
A trend or repeat you can see in data, such as rain on most afternoons or a run of dry days.

name: Prediction
defs: The system’s best guess about something it can’t know for sure — “this message is spam”, “this river will flood”. It can be about now, and it can be wrong.
A best guess about something the system doesn’t know yet, about the future or about now. It can be wrong.

name: Training data
defs: The examples a computer system learns from — for example, thousands of emails marked “spam” or “not spam”, or leaf photos labelled by experts.
The text a model learns from. Some tools may add users’ chats to it unless that setting is switched off.
The labelled examples a model learns from, such as messages tagged “safe” or “scam”.
The text a model learned from. It can only write from the patterns in it.

name: Label
defs: The answer that goes with an example, usually added by a person — such as “spam” or “not spam”, or the name of a leaf disease.
The right answer attached to an example, usually by a person.
The right answer that goes with an example, usually added by a person.
The name given to an example, like “mango” or “lemon”.
The answer attached to a training example, such as “healthy” or “sick”, that the model learns from.

name: Model
defs: What training produces: the patterns the computer found, stored as numbers. It takes a new example and gives a prediction, such as “probably spam”.
What training produces: the patterns the computer found, stored as numbers, ready to guess about new examples.
A simple rule learned from data that makes predictions.

name: Testing
defs: Checking a trained model on new examples it has never seen. We already know their labels, so we can count how often its predictions are right.

name: Bias (in AI)
defs: When an AI system works worse, or less fairly, for some groups of people than for others. It often starts with gaps in the examples it learned from.

name: Data gap
defs: When some people, places, accents or languages are missing — or very rare — in the examples an AI system learned from.
Kinds of people, voices or things missing from the examples, which make the AI fail more often for them.
A group of people, places or situations that is missing or too rare in the training data.

name: Varied (representative) examples
defs: Examples that match the people, places and things a tool will meet in real use — every group is there, with enough examples of each.

name: Chatbot (a type of generative AI)
asks: What is Chatbot (a type of generative AI)?
Can you explain Chatbot (a type of generative AI)?
I don't understand Chatbot (a type of generative AI).
What does Chatbot (a type of generative AI) mean?
Teach me Chatbot (a type of generative AI).
What is a type of generative AI?
defs: An AI tool that creates new text when you ask. It writes by predicting likely next words, using patterns from huge amounts of text.

name: Hallucination
defs: When an AI gives an answer that sounds sure and believable but is false — for example, a made-up fact, quote or source. The AI isn’t lying on purpose.
When AI states something false as if it were true, such as an invented date, quote or source.
When AI makes up something that sounds true but isn't.

name: Trusted source
defs: A place to check facts where a known person or organisation is responsible for getting them right — your textbook, an official website, or a colleague who knows the subject.
A source that is responsible for what it says: your textbook, your teacher, a ministry, a university or a well-known news organisation.

name: Trusting the machine too much (automation bias)
asks: What is Trusting the machine too much (automation bias)?
Can you explain Trusting the machine too much (automation bias)?
I don't understand Trusting the machine too much (automation bias).
What does Trusting the machine too much (automation bias) mean?
Teach me Trusting the machine too much (automation bias).
defs: Trusting a machine’s answer more than you should — accepting it without checking, even when it is wrong.

name: Large language model (LLM)
asks: Can you explain Large language model (LLM)?
I don't understand Large language model (LLM).
What does Large language model (LLM) mean?
defs: A program trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next token. A chatbot is an LLM trained further to hold a conversation.

name: Next-token prediction
defs: How a language model writes: it scores the possible next tokens, picks a likely one, adds it and repeats.

name: Knowledge cut-off
defs: The date a model’s training text ends. For anything newer it needs a web search, or a text you give it.

name: Prompt
defs: Everything you tell an AI tool to do: the request itself, plus any role, context, format and examples.
What you type to an AI: your question or request. A clear prompt gets a more useful answer.
What you type or say to an AI tool: a question, an instruction, or a text for it to work on.

name: Format
defs: How the answer should look: a numbered list, a table, a word limit, timings.

name: Follow-up
defs: A short message that improves the last answer, such as “Make it shorter”, instead of starting a new chat.
A reply that improves an answer instead of starting again, such as “shorter” or “give me another example”.

name: Grounding
defs: Tying an AI’s answer to a source you give it, such as a textbook page, so you know where each answer should come from.
Giving the model a trusted source and asking it to answer only from that. It lowers mistakes but doesn’t remove them.

name: RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)
defs: A tool first searches trusted documents, then answers from what it found and shows the source.

name: Bias
defs: When material favours or leaves out some people, or repeats stereotypes, such as showing every doctor as a man.
A starting push added to every total: how keen the neuron is to say yes. In a neuron it does not mean unfairness.
When a model makes more mistakes for one group of people than for others, usually because that group was missing or rare in its data.
Mistakes that fall more on one group than another.

name: Local fit
defs: Whether examples use your pupils’ own foods, names, money, seasons and places.

name: Anonymise
defs: Remove or replace everything that points to a person, for example writing Pupil A, B, C instead of names.
To remove names and any details that could identify a person, for example writing “Pupil A” instead of a name.

name: Age rules
defs: The minimum age a tool allows: often 13, some 18; under 18, often with a parent’s permission.

name: Artificial neuron
defs: A tiny calculation: multiply each input by its weight, add the bias, and turn the total into an answer. It is arithmetic, not a brain cell.

name: Weight
defs: How much an input matters to the decision. Big pushes hard, zero is ignored, negative pushes towards no.
How much a criterion counts in a decision. Weights are a choice about values, so they are agreed before the options are scored.

name: Training
defs: Adjusting the weights and bias a little at a time, so the neuron’s answers match the right ones more often.

name: Hidden layer
defs: Neurons between the inputs and the output. Each draws a line, and the next layer combines them into shapes one neuron can’t make.

name: Error
defs: A number for how far the network’s answer is from the right label. Training tries to make it small.

name: Gradient descent
defs: The training loop: guess, measure the error, nudge every weight a little downhill, repeat.

name: Learning rate
defs: The size of each training step. Too big and the error never settles; too small and training is slow.

name: Overfitting
defs: Learning the training examples so closely, noise included, that the model does worse on new ones.
When a model memorises its training examples: perfect on them, poor on new ones.
Fitting the noise in training data, so new data goes badly.
Fitting noise: low training error, high test error.

name: False positive
defs: A false alarm: the model says yes, but the true answer is no.
The model says yes when the answer is no: a false alarm, such as “sick” for a healthy leaf.

name: False negative
defs: A miss: the model says no, but the true answer is yes.
The model says no when the answer is yes: a miss, such as “healthy” for a sick leaf.

name: Attention
defs: The step where the newest token looks back at every earlier token and weighs which ones matter, gathering the context for the next word.

name: Pretraining
defs: The first stage: predicting the next token across huge amounts of text, nudging billions of weights after every miss.

name: AI audit
defs: A planned test of an AI tool on work like your pupils’, comparing its errors for each group before you decide to use it.

name: Overall accuracy
defs: The share of right answers across everyone tested. It is an average, so it can hide a group the tool fails.

name: Errors per group
asks: Can you explain Errors per group?
I don't understand Errors per group.
What does Errors per group mean?
defs: How often a tool is wrong for one group of pupils, such as village readers or girls. Comparing groups shows whether the tool is fair.

name: Pilot
defs: A trial of a tool in one class for a limited time, with a teacher checking its results, before the school decides.
One complete sensor node, run in its real place for a week or two before building more.

name: Principle
defs: A rule about why and how, not about which app — for example, “people stay responsible” — so it still applies when tools change.

name: Weighted decision matrix
asks: Can you explain Weighted decision matrix?
I don't understand Weighted decision matrix.
What does Weighted decision matrix mean?
defs: A table that scores each option on agreed criteria, multiplies each score by how much that criterion matters, and adds them up.

name: AI-writing detector
defs: A tool that guesses from patterns whether text was written by AI. It gives a score, not proof, and in studies it has wrongly flagged many second-language writers.
A tool that claims to spot writing done by AI. Detectors are unreliable: they can miss AI writing and wrongly flag real work.

name: False alarm
defs: When a detector flags something that isn’t there — here, calling an honest pupil’s own work AI.
When AI flags something harmless as a problem, such as a real message sent to spam.
When a detector flags honest work as written by AI.
When a guardrail blocks something harmless, such as a lesson that mentions passwords.
An alert when nothing is wrong. Too many, and people stop paying attention.
The alarm goes off, but nothing is wrong.

name: AI-use level
defs: A label on a task saying how much AI is allowed, from none to full use with an explanation.

name: Process evidence
defs: Plans, notes, drafts and talk that show how a pupil reached the final work.

name: Backward design
defs: Planning a unit from its learning goals and evidence first, and choosing activities and tools last.

name: No-device path
defs: A way for pupils without a phone or data to do the same activity: a printout, a phone shared in a group, or a demonstration.

name: Decision tree
defs: A model that decides through a chain of questions. Because every step can be read, pupils can see and question why it decides.

name: Unit evaluation
defs: Checking whether a unit worked — with quizzes before and after, pupils’ work and their views — and sharing the results with colleagues.

name: Rule-following machine
defs: A machine that does exactly what a person set, the same way every time, and never learns: an alarm, a calculator, a timer.

name: Test examples
defs: Labelled examples kept aside and never used in training, to check whether the model learned the patterns.

name: Pixel
defs: One tiny square of a digital picture, stored as a number (or three numbers for colour).
One tiny square of a picture, stored as about three numbers: red, green and blue.

name: Computer vision
defs: AI that learns patterns in pixel numbers from many labelled photos, then predicts what a new picture shows.

name: Edge
defs: A place in a picture where the numbers jump from light to dark: the simplest pattern vision AI looks for.

name: Miss
defs: When AI fails to flag something real, such as a scam that reaches your inbox.
A real problem with no alert. For a water tank, a day without water.
Something is wrong, but the alarm stays quiet.

name: Threshold
defs: The line a score must pass before the AI raises the alarm. People choose where it goes.
The score above which the model says yes.
The score above which the model says yes.
The number in a rule where the decision changes, such as “dark below 300”.
The number in a rule's condition, such as 30 °C or 1,000 ppm.
The value at which an alert switches on, such as 1,500 ppm of CO₂.
The number where a rule's decision changes, such as “dark below 50”.
The number in a rule where a device switches: fan on above 30 °C.

name: Language model
defs: A program trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next piece of writing. Chatbots are built on language models.

name: Cut-off date
defs: The date a model’s training text ends. Things that happened later can be missing, unless the chatbot searches the web.

name: Claim
defs: A single statement that can be checked: a number, a date, a name or a quote.
Something someone says is true, often with a number.

name: Deepfake
defs: A photo, video or voice made or changed by AI to look or sound real.
A photo, voice or video made with AI to look real. Check before you share, and never make one of a real person.
A photo, voice or video made or changed with AI to look real.
A photo, video or voice made or changed by AI to look or sound real.
A video, picture or voice made or changed with AI so that it looks or sounds like a real person.

name: Honest use
defs: Using AI to help you learn (explain, quiz, check) within your school’s rules, and saying how you used it.

name: Copying (plagiarism)
defs: Handing in work that an AI, or anyone else, did as if it were yours, even with a few words changed.

name: AI-use note
defs: A short line on your work saying how you used AI, such as “to explain fractions”.

name: Dataset
defs: All the labelled examples a model learns from, such as forty leaf photos, each marked “healthy” or “sick”.

name: Balanced data
defs: A dataset with about the same number of examples of each label, so a model can’t look good by always giving one answer.

name: Permission
defs: A person’s agreement before you collect their voice, photo or work, after you have told them what it is for.
Agreement, given before you start, from the people who own the data or are described in it.
An app’s request to use part of your phone, such as the camera, microphone, contacts or location. You can allow or refuse it, and change your mind in Settings.
Your yes to an app using something on your phone, like your location, camera or contacts. You can take it back at any time in Settings.
Your OK for an app to use the camera, microphone, location or contacts. Allow only what it needs.

name: Classifier
defs: A model that puts a new example into one of several classes, such as “ripe” or “not ripe”.

name: Feature
defs: A number you can measure about every example in the same way, such as softness from 0 to 10.
A measured property used by the model.

name: Nearest neighbours
defs: A way to classify: find the stored examples most like the new one, and go with the label most of them have.
Giving a new case the most common label of the k closest examples.

name: Overall score
defs: One score for all the test examples together. It can look good while hiding a group the model fails.

name: Testing by group
asks: Can you explain Testing by group?
I don't understand Testing by group.
What does Testing by group mean?
defs: Counting right and wrong answers separately for each group, so a gap can’t hide.

name: AI ethics
defs: Asking whether an AI is right to use, not only whether it works: who gains, who could be harmed, and who gets a say.

name: Consent
defs: Agreeing to something after being told what it does, with a real choice to say no.
Clear permission, usually written, from a parent (and, for older pupils, the pupil) before a photo or personal detail is shared. It can be withdrawn.
Saying yes freely. Ask for it before you post someone, and respect a no.
Clear permission, given freely, for a stated use; for children, usually from a parent or guardian.
Agreement, freely given, after people are told what is collected and why. For children, from their parents too.

name: Task
defs: One piece of a job. AI usually changes some tasks in a job rather than the whole job.

name: Automation
defs: When AI or a machine does a task instead of a person, such as a filter sorting spam.

name: Augmentation
defs: When AI helps a person do a task better, and the person still decides, such as an alert that helps a nurse.

name: Data labelling
defs: Giving each example its right answer, such as “sick” or “healthy” for a leaf photo, so a model can learn. It is real work done by people.

name: Design plan
defs: A short plan under five headings: whose problem, is AI needed, what data with whose permission, what the AI does, and what happens when it’s wrong.

name: Safeguard
defs: A step that stops a mistake from causing harm, such as showing the source or saying “I don’t know”.

name: Person in charge
asks: Can you explain Person in charge?
I don't understand Person in charge.
What does Person in charge mean?
defs: A named person who checks the AI, fixes its mistakes and makes the important decisions.

name: Paper prototype
defs: A design drawn on paper, one screen per sheet, that you test with real users before writing any code.

name: User testing
defs: Watching real users try your design, without helping, to find where they get stuck.

name: Explainable AI
defs: An AI whose decisions a person can follow and explain in plain words, like a decision tree.

name: Pitch
defs: A short talk, about two minutes, that explains your idea and why it can be trusted, risks included.

name: Chat history
defs: The record of your past conversations that an AI service keeps, often on its servers and on your device.

name: Data traffic light
asks: Can you explain Data traffic light?
I don't understand Data traffic light.
What does Data traffic light mean?
defs: Green: no person in it. Amber: only with names and details taken out. Red: never type it.

name: Stakes ladder
defs: Low stakes: read it. Medium: check the textbook. High: an expert or official source, and a person decides.

name: Automation bias
defs: Trusting an answer more because a machine gave it.

name: Official source
defs: The body that owns the facts: the exam board, the ministry, a health service, the school.

name: Voice clone
defs: A copy of someone's voice made by AI from a short recording.

name: Second channel
defs: A way of checking you already trust, such as a saved number or the school's usual group, not the message itself.
A different way of checking, one you already trust, such as calling back on a saved number.

name: Code word
defs: A word agreed in advance with family or colleagues, asked for before acting on any request about money.

name: AI detector
defs: A tool that guesses from patterns whether a text was written by AI. Its score is a guess, not proof.

name: Watermark
defs: A hidden preference for certain words that a model adds while writing, so a detector with the key can spot it later.
The latest timestamp already loaded; an incremental load takes only newer rows.

name: Class rules for AI
asks: What is Class rules for AI?
Can you explain Class rules for AI?
I don't understand Class rules for AI.
What does Class rules for AI mean?
Teach me Class rules for AI.
defs: Keep it out, check it, verify it, be fair, tell someone.

name: Prompt injection
defs: Instructions hidden in text an AI reads, which it may follow as if they came from you.
Hiding an order where an AI will read it, so that it follows the order or passes it on.
Orders hidden in text an AI app reads (a web page, a document, a tool's result), hoping the model follows them.

name: Direct injection
defs: An instruction typed straight into the chat by the person using the AI.

name: Indirect injection
defs: An instruction hidden in content the AI reads: a document, an email, a web page or a tool's result.
An order hidden in something the AI reads, such as a web page, a document or a message, not typed by you.

name: Untrusted content
defs: Anything the AI reads that someone else wrote. Treat it as data, never as orders.

name: Jailbreak
defs: An attempt to talk a chatbot round its safety rules, usually by rewording a request it would refuse.
An attempt to talk a chatbot past its rules, by hunting for a wording its training missed.
An attempt to talk a chatbot out of the rules it was trained to keep, with new wordings, role play or many turns.

name: Safety training
defs: Extra training that teaches a model to refuse harmful requests. It is learned, so it doesn't cover every wording.

name: Red teaming
defs: Testing a system on purpose, with permission, by trying what it should refuse and recording what gets through.
Trying, on purpose and with permission, the things a system should refuse, to find its weaknesses before others do.

name: Severity
defs: How bad a finding is, often rated 1 (low) to 3 (high), so the worst gets fixed first.
How bad a miss is: 1 embarrassing, 2 harmful, 3 a danger to a person or their data.

name: Keyword filter
defs: A guardrail that blocks text containing words from a list. It misses rewording and blocks innocent text.
A guard that blocks text containing words from a list. Easy to write; it misses rewording and blocks innocent text.

name: Action check
defs: Code that lets an action happen only if a person asked for it and approved it, whatever the wording.
A rule in code that lets an action happen only if the user asked for it and approved it, whatever the wording.

name: Blast radius
defs: Everything a tricked agent could reach or change with the tools it holds.
Everything an attack could reach through the tools and data an agent holds.
Everything an attacker could reach or do if one part is tricked. Least privilege keeps it small.

name: Human approval
defs: A person's yes to an exact action, checked in code before the action happens.

name: Data poisoning
defs: Slipping wrong or planted examples into training data so that a model learns the wrong thing.
Adding wrong examples on purpose to spoil what an AI learns.
Slipping wrong or planted examples into training data, so the model learns something wrong.

name: Backdoor
defs: A hidden trigger planted through training: the model behaves normally until the trigger appears, then gives the attacker's answer.
A hidden trigger planted in training data: the model behaves normally until the trigger appears.

name: Median
defs: The middle value once a list is sorted. One bad value barely moves it, unlike the average.
The middle value once the values are sorted. One wild value hardly moves it.
The middle value once the numbers are sorted. One extreme value hardly moves it.
The middle value when the values are in order.
The middle value when the list is in order.
The middle value of the sorted readings. A few wild readings barely move it.
The middle value when readings are put in order. One bad reading barely moves it.
The middle reading when they are put in order; one glitch barely moves it.

name: Clean test set
asks: Can you explain Clean test set?
I don't understand Clean test set.
What does Clean test set mean?
defs: Checked examples kept apart and never changed, used to compare a model's score before and after new data.
Checked examples kept locked away and used only to score the model, so a sudden drop warns you.

name: Memorisation
defs: When a model stores a training example almost exactly and can repeat it, instead of only learning patterns.

name: Membership inference
defs: Guessing whether a person's data was used to train a model, from how familiar the model finds it.
Guessing whether a person's record was in a model's training data, often from how confident the model is.

name: Redaction
defs: Removing identifiers such as names, numbers and addresses from text before it is used or shared.

name: Canary
defs: A made-up secret planted in training data to test whether a model memorises and repeats what it saw.

name: Adversarial example
defs: An input changed on purpose, often only slightly, so that a model gets it wrong while people see no difference.
An input changed a little, on purpose, so a model gets it wrong while people see no difference.

name: Adversarial training
defs: Making tricky examples on purpose, labelling them correctly and training on them, so a model is harder to fool.

name: Confidence
defs: The score a model gives its own answer. It is not a guarantee: a model can be sure and wrong.

name: Fragile answer
defs: An answer that changes when the input is nudged a tiny amount; it shouldn't decide anything alone.

name: Supply chain
defs: Everyone whose work an AI tool depends on: data, model, code libraries, plug-ins and the app itself.
All the parts an AI tool is built from, made by others: data, model files, code, apps and plug-ins.

name: Fingerprint (hash)
defs: A short code computed from a file, such as SHA-256's 64 characters. Change one byte and it changes completely.

name: Digital signature
defs: Made with the maker's private key and checked with their public key: it shows who published a file and that it hasn't changed.
Proof, made with the publisher's secret key and checked with their public key, that a file really comes from them.
Proof, made with a private key, of who sent a message and that it hasn’t changed since.

name: Tool inventory
defs: A school's list of the AI tools it uses: name, version, source, fingerprint and who approved it.

name: Threat model
defs: A short, written answer to: what are we protecting, what could go wrong, what will we do about it, and did it work?
A structured look at a system: what it is, what can go wrong, what you'll do about it, and whether that worked.

name: Inventory
defs: The list of every AI tool in use, with the data it touches, what it can do, who uses it and who looks after it.

name: Untrusted input
defs: Anything an AI reads that you didn't write: web pages, essays, messages, tool results. It may carry a hidden order or a mistake.

name: Risk score
defs: Likelihood (1–3) × impact (1–3). The highest scores are dealt with first.

name: Test bank
defs: The list of requests you test, each in more than one wording, with the response that would be right.

name: Responsible disclosure
defs: Reporting a weakness to the owner first, giving them time to fix it, and never publishing a recipe for the attack.
Reporting a flaw privately to its owner, giving time to fix it, and sharing the lesson afterwards, never a working exploit.
Telling the owner about a weakness privately, and not testing it further or sharing it, so it can be fixed safely.

name: Approved tool
defs: An AI tool the school has checked (data, age, powers, law) and allows, with a named person who looks after it.

name: Enforced check
defs: A rule built into the system (a setting, a permission, an approval step, a line of code), so it holds without anyone having to remember it.

name: AI incident
defs: Something going wrong with AI that harms, or could harm, people or data: a leak, a fake, harmful advice, an action nobody approved.

name: Containment
defs: The first steps that stop the harm growing: pausing the tool, deleting the data, removing posts, changing passwords.

name: Data breach
defs: Personal data reaching people who shouldn't have it. Many laws require serious breaches to be reported to the regulator, often within 72 hours.

name: Incident drill
defs: A short practice in which staff talk through an imagined incident and decide each step, so the real one is handled calmly.

name: AI (artificial intelligence)
defs: A computer program that learns from lots of examples and then makes guesses.

name: Chatbot
defs: An AI you can type or talk to, which answers in words.

name: Guess
defs: An answer that might be right, but nobody has checked it.

name: Example
defs: Something an AI learns from, like a picture of a fruit.

name: Odd one out
asks: Can you explain Odd one out?
I don't understand Odd one out.
What does Odd one out mean?
defs: An example that doesn't look like the others with the same label.

name: Secret
defs: Something about you that only you and your family should know, like your address or your password.

name: Smart toy
defs: A toy that can listen and talk, and may send what you say to a computer far away.

name: Privacy
defs: Keeping your secrets safe, and choosing who knows things about you.

name: Fake
defs: A picture, voice, video or message made to look real when it isn't.

name: Scam
defs: A trick to get your money, your secrets or your password.
A trick to get your money, password, code or personal details, usually by pretending to be someone you trust or by offering something amazing.

name: Family code word
asks: Can you explain Family code word?
I don't understand Family code word.
What does Family code word mean?
defs: A secret word your family chooses, to check that a caller is really one of you.
A word only your family knows and never posts, asked for when a call or message wants money or help in a hurry.

name: Stop, think, ask
asks: Can you explain Stop, think, ask?
I don't understand Stop, think, ask.
What does Stop, think, ask mean?
defs: A habit for anything strange: don't act yet, think who sent it, show a grown-up.

name: Voice cloning
defs: Copying how a person sounds from a recording of their voice, sometimes a very short one.

name: Reverse image search
asks: Can you explain Reverse image search?
I don't understand Reverse image search.
What does Reverse image search mean?
defs: Searching with a picture instead of words, to find where it appeared first.

name: Watermark (in AI content)
asks: Can you explain Watermark (in AI content)?
I don't understand Watermark (in AI content).
What does Watermark (in AI content) mean?
defs: A hidden signal an AI tool puts in what it makes, so a detector with the key can guess it was machine-made.

name: One-time code
defs: A short code sent to your phone to sign in or approve something. It is a key: never share it.
A short code sent to your phone to prove it is really you. It works once, for a short time. Never give it to anyone.
A short code, sent by text or made by an app, that works once and only for a short time. It’s for you alone.

name: Fake app
defs: An app that copies a famous one to steal logins, show adverts or read your data.

name: Source
defs: The real page, video or document a summary was made from. Check the summary against it.

name: Word filter
defs: A guardrail that blocks text containing words on a list. Rewording gets past it.

name: Check on the action
asks: What is Check on the action?
Can you explain Check on the action?
I don't understand Check on the action.
What does Check on the action mean?
Teach me Check on the action.
defs: A rule in code that lets an app act, for example send a message, only if you asked and said yes.

name: Fingerprint (SHA-256)
defs: 64 hex characters computed from a file's bytes. Any change to the file changes about half of it.

name: Model list
defs: A record of the models and AI tools you use: name, version, where each came from and its fingerprint.

name: Trust boundary
defs: A line where data you don't control enters a part you do control.

name: STRIDE
defs: Six kinds of threat to check at each boundary: spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege.

name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications
asks: What is OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications?
Can you explain OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications?
I don't understand OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications.
What does OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications mean?
Teach me OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications.
defs: A free, widely used list of the ten biggest security risks in apps built on language models (2025 edition).

name: Improper output handling
asks: Can you explain Improper output handling?
I don't understand Improper output handling.
What does Improper output handling mean?
defs: Using a model's reply downstream (in a page, a query, a command) without checking or escaping it.

name: Escaping
defs: Turning special characters into harmless codes, such as < into <, so they are shown, not run.

name: System prompt
defs: The hidden instructions an app gives its model. Assume they can be read, so keep secrets out of them.

name: Fast gradient sign method (FGSM)
asks: What is Fast gradient sign method (FGSM)?
Can you explain Fast gradient sign method (FGSM)?
I don't understand Fast gradient sign method (FGSM).
What does Fast gradient sign method (FGSM) mean?
Teach me Fast gradient sign method (FGSM).
defs: Move every input a small step ε in the direction that raises the model's error most: against the weight's sign in a linear model.

name: Model extraction
defs: Copying a model by querying it many times and training a look-alike on its answers.

name: Rules of engagement
asks: Can you explain Rules of engagement?
I don't understand Rules of engagement.
What does Rules of engagement mean?
defs: What a red team agreed in writing before testing: permission, scope, test data, a stop rule and a contact.

name: Evaluation harness
defs: Code that runs a bank of test cases, grades each one and reports a pass rate for each category.

name: Algorithm
defs: A list of precise steps, in order, that finishes and solves a problem.
A list of exact steps, in order.

name: Program
defs: An algorithm written so a computer can run it: in cards, blocks or code.
A list of exact instructions that a computer runs one line at a time, from the top down.

name: Sequence
defs: Steps done one after another, in order. Change the order and the result changes.

name: Exact (unambiguous)
defs: Meaning only one thing. “Turn right” is exact; “go over there” is not.

name: Loop
defs: Steps said once, with how many times (or until when) to repeat them.
Lines that repeat. for repeats once per value; while repeats while a condition is true.
Steps you say once, with how many times to repeat them.
The part of a program that repeats: read, decide, act, wait.
The part of a program that repeats forever: read, decide, act, wait.

name: Repeat count
defs: How many times a loop runs. Change it, and the whole program changes with one edit.

name: For each
defs: A loop that runs once for every item in a list, such as every pupil in the register.

name: Condition
defs: Something that is either true or false: “it is raining”, “the robot is facing a wall”.
Something a sensor can check, true or false right now: the room is above 30 °C.

name: IF … THEN … ELSE
asks: Can you explain IF … THEN … ELSE?
I don't understand IF … THEN … ELSE.
What does IF … THEN … ELSE mean?
defs: A decision: do one thing if the condition is true, another if it is false.

name: AND, OR
defs: Join conditions. AND needs both to be true; OR needs at least one.

name: Bug, debugging
defs: A mistake in a program, and the routine of finding and fixing it: test, find the first wrong step, change one thing, test again.

name: Decomposition
defs: Breaking a big problem into smaller parts you can solve one at a time.

name: Pattern recognition
defs: Noticing what repeats or is the same, so one solution can be used again.

name: Abstraction
defs: Keeping what matters for the job and leaving out the details that don’t.

name: Halving (binary search)
defs: Guess the middle and throw away the half it can’t be in. It needs the items in order.

name: Variable
defs: A name that holds one value at a time. The equals sign stores a value in it: mark = 14.
A name that holds one value at a time. = stores a value in it.
A number the model chooses, with a meaning and a unit, such as cups of rice per pupil.
A letter for a number you choose, with a unit, such as r = cups of rice.

name: Text (a string)
defs: Letters, digits or spaces inside quotes. "53" is text; 53 is a number.
Letters or numbers inside quotes, shown exactly as written: "7 + 3".

name: input() and int()
asks: Can you explain input() and int()?
I don't understand input() and int().
What does input() and int() mean?
defs: input() asks a question and gives back what is typed, as text. int() turns text such as "12" into the number 12.

name: Comparison
defs: A test that is True or False, such as mark >= 50. == compares; = stores.
A test that is True or False, such as age < 12. == compares; = stores.

name: if, elif and else
asks: What is if, elif and else?
Can you explain if, elif and else?
I don't understand if, elif and else.
What does if, elif and else mean?
Teach me if, elif and else.
defs: Choices checked from the top: only the first true branch runs; else catches the rest.

name: Indent
defs: The 4 spaces at the start of the lines that belong to an if, elif, else, for or while.

name: Boundary
defs: A value where the answer changes, such as 49 and 50 for a pass mark of 50. Test there first.
A value where the answer changes, like 12 for “under 12”. Test there.

name: range(a, b)
defs: The whole numbers from a up to, but not including, b: range(1, 5) is 1, 2, 3, 4.
The numbers from a up to, but not including, b.

name: Running total
defs: A variable set to 0 before a loop and added to on every turn: total = total + n.

name: Off by one
asks: Can you explain Off by one?
I don't understand Off by one.
What does Off by one mean?
defs: A loop that runs one time too many or too few, usually because range stops before its second number.

name: List
defs: Many values under one name, in order, inside square brackets: [14, 9, 17].
In Python, values in square brackets, such as [14, 9, 17].

name: Index
defs: A value’s position in a list, counting from 0. marks[0] is the first; marks[-1] the last.
A position in a list, from 0; -1 is the last item.
A sorted copy of one column with a pointer to each row, so lookups can halve.

name: len, sum, max, min
asks: What is len, sum, max, min?
Can you explain len, sum, max, min?
I don't understand len, sum, max, min.
What does len, sum, max, min mean?
Teach me len, sum, max, min.
defs: How many values, their total, the highest and the lowest.

name: CSV file
defs: A table saved as text, one row per line, with commas between the values: Amina,14.
A table saved as plain text: one line per row, commas between the values, the column names first.

name: PRIMM
defs: Predict, Run, Investigate, Modify, Make: a lesson structure that puts reading code before writing it.

name: Trace table
defs: A table with a column per variable and a row per line that runs, filled in by hand.
A column per variable and a row per step, filled in by hand to follow a program.

name: Predict question
defs: “What will this print?”, with wrong answers that each reveal a misconception.

name: Use–Modify–Create
defs: Use a working program, change it, then make your own: the same idea as PRIMM, over a project.

name: Parsons problem
defs: The lines of a working program, shuffled: put them in order and indent them.

name: Distractor
defs: A line that doesn’t belong, built from a real misconception, such as if mark = 50:.

name: One correct order
asks: Can you explain One correct order?
I don't understand One correct order.
What does One correct order mean?
defs: No two lines that could swap: each line depends on the one before.

name: Fill the gaps
asks: Can you explain Fill the gaps?
I don't understand Fill the gaps.
What does Fill the gaps mean?
defs: The next step after Parsons: most of the code is given, and pupils write the key parts.

name: Error message
defs: Python’s report: the kind of error and the line. The mistake is on that line or just before it.
Python’s clue when something is wrong: the kind of error and its line number.

name: Logic error
defs: A bug with no error message: the program runs but gives the wrong answer.

name: Print debugging
defs: Printing values in the middle of a program to see where they go wrong.

name: Rubber duck debugging
asks: Can you explain Rubber duck debugging?
I don't understand Rubber duck debugging.
What does Rubber duck debugging mean?
defs: Explaining the code aloud, line by line, until the wrong line shows itself.

name: Misconception
defs: A reasonable but wrong idea about how code works, shared by many pupils.

name: Hinge question
defs: One quick question at a lesson’s turning point; each wrong answer shows a particular misconception.

name: Diagnostic distractor
defs: A wrong option written to catch one misconception, so the answer tells you what to reteach.

name: Feedback that asks
asks: Can you explain Feedback that asks?
I don't understand Feedback that asks.
What does Feedback that asks mean?
defs: A question that sends the pupil back to their code, instead of a fix.

name: Unplugged
defs: Teaching a computing idea with cards, chalk, string and people, without screens.

name: Binary cards
defs: Cards with 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 dots: face up or down, they show a number in binary.

name: Sorting network
defs: Lines drawn on the floor where pupils compare and swap, acting out a sorting algorithm.

name: Then plugged
defs: Linking the activity to code or an app soon after, so pupils see the same idea on a computer.

name: Pair programming
defs: Two pupils, one device: a driver and a navigator who swap every 5 to 10 minutes.

name: Group roles
defs: For four pupils and one phone: driver, navigator, tester and reporter, swapped each task.

name: Live coding
defs: Writing code in front of the class, pausing for predictions, mistakes included.

name: Offline ready
defs: Lessons downloaded and Python saved once, so everything works with no connection.

name: Desk check
defs: Tracing someone’s code by hand, before running it, to find bugs.

name: Paper assessment
defs: Predict, order, trace, find the bug, write by hand: fair to every pupil, device or not.

name: Worksheet
defs: Darsi’s printed kit: each lesson’s first questions and code steps as paper exercises.

name: Scheme of work
asks: Can you explain Scheme of work?
I don't understand Scheme of work.
What does Scheme of work mean?
defs: The plan for a subject across the year: units, order, timing and how learning is checked.

name: Progression
defs: The order of ideas across grades, each building on the last: unplugged, blocks, then Python.

name: Assessment point
defs: A planned check at the end of a unit: a quiz, a Parsons task or a short program.

name: Device timetable
defs: Who gets the school’s devices, and when, so no class waits a whole term.

name: Instruction
defs: One step that tells a robot or a computer what to do, such as “turn left”.

name: Order
defs: Which step comes first, next and last. Change it, and the result changes.

name: Repeat
defs: Doing the same step again. A card can repeat up to 4 times.
The same record typed twice, such as the same pupil on the same day. Find repeats after the names agree.
The same thing counted twice, such as one reading sent two times.

name: Decision
defs: IF something is true, THEN do this, ELSE do that.

name: AND
defs: Both things must be true.
On only when all inputs are on. Two switches in series.
1 only when all inputs are 1. Switches in series.

name: OR
defs: One true thing is enough.
On when any input is on. Two switches in parallel.
1 when any input is 1. Switches in parallel.

name: Test every case
asks: Can you explain Test every case?
I don't understand Test every case.
What does Test every case mean?
defs: Try every possible mix (yes and no) to check the rule always works.

name: Bug
defs: A mistake in a program. Everyone makes them.

name: Debugging
defs: Finding and fixing a bug: run it, find the first wrong step, change one thing, run it again.

name: Program in words
asks: Can you explain Program in words?
I don't understand Program in words.
What does Program in words mean?
defs: The robot’s cards written as words: forward(2), left(), right().

name: print()
defs: Shows text or a value on the screen.

name: Operators
defs: + add, - subtract, * multiply, / divide, ** power. * and / come first.

name: input()
defs: Asks a question and gives back what is typed, always as text.

name: int()
defs: Turns text such as "13" into the number 13, so you can do maths with it.
Turns text such as “14” into the number 14, so it can be added up.

name: NameError, TypeError
defs: A name Python doesn’t know (often a typo), and text mixed with a number.

name: if, elif, else
asks: Can you explain if, elif, else?
I don't understand if, elif, else.
What does if, elif, else mean?
defs: Choices checked from the top: only the first true one runs.

name: and, or
defs: and: both must be true. or: one is enough.

name: for loop
defs: Repeats once for each value: for i in range(1, 6):.

name: while loop
defs: Repeats as long as its condition is True.

name: Endless loop
defs: A loop whose condition never becomes False. Something inside must change.

name: Parameter, argument
defs: The names a function expects (length, width) and the values a call gives them (4, 3).

name: return
defs: Hands a result back to the caller. print only shows it; a function with no return gives None.

name: assert
defs: A test: assert area(4, 3) == 12 stops with an AssertionError if the answer is wrong.

name: Slice
defs: Part of a list: temps[1:3] is the items at 1 and 2.

name: append, pop
defs: Add to the end; take from the end (pop()) or the front (pop(0)).

name: Stack, queue
defs: Last in, first out (undo); first in, first out (a line).

name: Linear search
defs: Check items one by one; return the position, or -1. Works on any list.
Reading row by row until the value is found: about half the table on average.

name: Binary search
defs: Look at the middle and throw away the half that can’t hold the target. Needs a sorted list.
Halving a sorted list at every look: about 20 looks for a million.

name: Worst case
defs: The most work an algorithm can need: 1,000 looks for linear search, about 10 for binary, with 1,000 items.

name: lo, mid, hi
asks: Can you explain lo, mid, hi?
I don't understand lo, mid, hi.
What does lo, mid, hi mean?
defs: The markers of binary search: the part still possible runs from lo to hi; mid is its middle.

name: Bubble sort
defs: Swap neighbours that are out of order, pass after pass: about n × n comparisons.

name: Insertion sort
defs: Slide each new item back into its place. Fast on nearly sorted lists.

name: Merge sort
defs: Sort each half, then merge them: about n × log n comparisons.

name: Edge case
defs: An unusual input where code often breaks: empty, one item, sorted, reversed, repeats.
An input at the limits: empty, one item, first or last, missing, negative, the boundary.

name: Big O
defs: How the number of steps grows with the input size n, ignoring constant factors.

name: O(n)
defs: Linear: one pass over the data. Double n, double the work.

name: O(n²)
defs: Quadratic: a loop inside a loop over the same data. Double n, four times the work.

name: O(log n)
defs: Logarithmic: halving at each step. A million items need about 20 steps.

name: Recursion
defs: A function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of it.

name: Base case
defs: The case answered at once, without another call. Every call must move towards it.

name: Call stack
defs: Where waiting calls sit. About 150 deep on the phone, 1,000 in desktop Python.

name: Memoisation
defs: Storing answers in a dictionary so each is worked out only once.

name: Stack
defs: Last in, first out: append to push, pop() to take the newest.

name: Queue
defs: First in, first out: join at the back, leave from the front (collections.deque for big ones).

name: Set
defs: Unique items; x in s takes about one step.
A Python collection that keeps each value only once: handy for counting different names.

name: Dictionary
defs: Values found by key in about one step: count[w] = count.get(w, 0) + 1.
A Python collection of keys and values, such as names by pupil ID; .get(key, "?") looks a key up safely.

name: Unit test
defs: A check of one small piece of code against a known answer: assert f(x) == expected.

name: Red, green, refactor
asks: Can you explain Red, green, refactor?
I don't understand Red, green, refactor.
What does Red, green, refactor mean?
defs: Test-first: a failing test, the simplest code that passes, then tidy with every test green.

name: Code review
defs: A second person reads each small change; comments are about the code, not the coder.

name: Passphrase
defs: A password made of several words, such as three random words joined together. It is long and hard to guess, but easy to picture and remember.
A long password made of several random words. Length makes it hard to guess and easy to remember.
A password made of three or four random words joined together: long, hard to guess and easy to remember.
A password made of several random words. Long, hard to guess and easy to remember.
Four or more random words joined together: long, hard to guess and easy to remember.

name: PIN
defs: Personal identification number: a short number code that protects a phone, a bank card or a mobile money account. Only you should know it.

name: Reusing a password
asks: Can you explain Reusing a password?
I don't understand Reusing a password.
What does Reusing a password mean?
defs: Using the same password for more than one account. If one website is hacked, criminals try that password on your other accounts too.

name: Phishing
defs: A message that pretends to come from someone you trust, like a bank or ministry, to trick you into clicking, paying or sharing secrets.
A scam message that pretends to come from someone you trust, like a game company, a bank or a friend, to make you click, log in or pay.

name: Link
defs: Words or a web address you tap to open a page. A phishing link can open a fake page that looks real and asks for your password.

name: Attachment
defs: A file sent with a message, such as a document or photo. An unexpected attachment can hide software that harms your phone or steals data.

name: Another channel
defs: A different way to reach the real person or company, like calling a number you already have. Never use the number or link in the message.
A different way to reach the real person or company, like a number you already know or the official app.

name: Screen lock
defs: A PIN, pattern, password, fingerprint or face check that must be passed before anyone can use your phone.

name: Update
defs: A free improvement from the phone or app maker. Many updates fix security holes that criminals could use to get in.
New software from the maker that fixes weak spots. Turn automatic updates on.
A fix from the maker that closes security holes. Turn on automatic updates.

name: App permission
defs: What an app is allowed to use on your phone, such as the camera, microphone, contacts, location or messages.

name: Backup
defs: A copy of your photos and contacts kept somewhere else — online or on a computer — so they survive if your phone is lost or broken.
A second copy of your files kept somewhere else, so you can get them back if the original is lost or damaged.

name: Admin
defs: A group member who can change the group’s settings, add or remove members, and approve people who ask to join.

name: Two-step verification
defs: An extra lock on your account. In WhatsApp, it’s a six-digit PIN you choose, asked for when your number is set up on a phone.

name: Privacy setting
defs: A choice in the app’s settings about who can see or do something — for example, who can add you to a group.

name: Impersonation
defs: Pretending to be someone else, such as putting a head teacher’s name and photo on a new number to ask for money.
An account or page pretending to be a real person or organisation, such as a fake school page asking for fees.

name: Security update
defs: A fix from the maker that closes a hole in software. The sooner it is installed, the less time a criminal has to use the hole.

name: Vulnerability
defs: A mistake in software that lets someone do what they shouldn’t, such as get in or take control.

name: End of support
asks: Can you explain End of support?
I don't understand End of support.
What does End of support mean?
defs: The date after which a device or system gets no more security updates. After it, new holes stay open.

name: Cracked software
defs: A paid program with its protection removed and shared for free. It often hides malware.

name: The 3-2-1 rule
defs: Three copies, on two kinds of storage, with one copy kept away from the building.

name: Ransomware
defs: Malware that locks your files and demands money to unlock them. An unplugged backup takes away its power.
Malware that locks your files and demands payment. A backup is the real cure.

name: Hash
defs: A short fingerprint computed from a file. Change one letter and the fingerprint changes completely, so it shows whether a copy is exact.

name: Two-step sign-in
defs: Signing in with two kinds of proof, such as a password and a code from your phone, so a stolen password alone isn’t enough.
Signing in with your password plus a second step, such as a code, a prompt on your phone or your fingerprint.

name: Authenticator app
defs: An app that makes a new sign-in code every 30 seconds, on your own phone, without text messages.

name: Passkey
defs: A way to sign in with your phone’s fingerprint, face or screen lock. It works only on the real site, so it can’t be phished.
A way to sign in with your fingerprint, face or the PIN that unlocks your phone, instead of a password. It only works on the real website, so a fake site can’t trick you out of it.

name: SIM swap
defs: A fraud in which a criminal gets your number moved to their SIM card, so your text message codes go to them.

name: HTTPS (the padlock)
defs: A private connection to a website: others on the network see the site’s name, but not what you send. It doesn’t prove the site is honest.

name: Hotspot
defs: A Wi-Fi network that anyone can create, from a router or a phone, and name as they like.

name: VPN
defs: A service that sends your traffic through a tunnel, hiding it from the local network but not from the VPN company.

name: Guest network
defs: A separate Wi-Fi network for visitors, kept apart from the computers that hold records.

name: Sensitive data
defs: Personal data that can cause special harm if it leaks, such as health, religion, or a family’s money or problems. It needs the most care.
Personal data that can do special harm if shared, such as health, disability, religion or family problems.

name: Collect less (data minimisation)
asks: Can you explain Collect less (data minimisation)?
I don't understand Collect less (data minimisation).
What does Collect less (data minimisation) mean?
defs: Collecting only the data a clear purpose needs, and nothing “just in case”.

name: Data protection law
asks: Can you explain Data protection law?
I don't understand Data protection law.
What does Data protection law mean?
defs: A country’s law on how organisations, schools included, may collect, use, keep and share personal data.

name: Minimum age
defs: The youngest age an app or service allows. Many set it at 13, and younger teens usually need a parent’s permission.

name: Private window
defs: A browser window that doesn’t keep your history or sign-ins after you close it. Files you download stay on the computer, and it doesn’t hide what you do from the network or from spying software.

name: Location tag
defs: Information a phone can store inside a photo file about where it was taken. You can turn it off in the camera’s settings.

name: Digital footprint
defs: Everything a person leaves online, posted by them or by others. Small details in it can add up.
All the traces you leave online, on purpose or not: posts, photos, searches, likes and places.

name: Data incident
defs: Any time personal data is lost, stolen, or seen or changed by people who shouldn’t: a lost phone, a message to the wrong group, a hacked account.

name: Contain
defs: The first step: stopping the damage from spreading, such as deleting a message for everyone or locking a lost phone.

name: Regulator
defs: The official body that enforces a country’s data protection law. Serious breaches may have to be reported to it, often within a deadline.

name: Incident log
defs: A simple record of each incident: the date, what happened, what data, who was told, and what changed.

name: Cyber safety policy
asks: Can you explain Cyber safety policy?
I don't understand Cyber safety policy.
What does Cyber safety policy mean?
defs: The school’s agreed rules for accounts, devices, data, groups and incidents, with a named person for each job.

name: Cyber lead
defs: The named person who keeps the policy up to date and whom staff tell when something goes wrong. A deputy covers when they are away.

name: Acceptable use agreement
asks: Can you explain Acceptable use agreement?
I don't understand Acceptable use agreement.
What does Acceptable use agreement mean?
defs: A short version of the rules that staff, pupils or parents sign, so everyone knows what is expected of them.

name: Asset
defs: Anything worth protecting: records, exam papers, accounts, devices, the school’s page.

name: Likelihood and impact
asks: Can you explain Likelihood and impact?
I don't understand Likelihood and impact.
What does Likelihood and impact mean?
defs: How likely something is to happen, and how bad it would be if it did. Each is scored from 1 to 3.

name: Control
defs: Something you do to lower a risk: prevent it, detect it fast, or recover from it.

name: Risk register
defs: A simple table of risks with their scores, controls, owners and dates, reviewed every term.

name: Tabletop exercise
defs: A drill in which staff talk through an imaginary incident around a table, step by step, with no computers.

name: Update (inject)
defs: A new piece of the story read out during a drill, which makes the situation harder and forces new decisions.

name: Communications lead
defs: The one person who speaks for the school during an incident, so parents get one clear message.

name: No-blame culture
defs: A school where people report mistakes early because they know they won’t be punished for reporting.

name: Spiral curriculum
defs: Teaching the same ideas again every year, with more depth as pupils grow.

name: Safeguarding lead
defs: The person at school who receives concerns about a pupil’s safety and follows the procedure with them.

name: Sextortion
defs: Blackmail in which someone threatens to share intimate images unless they are paid or sent more. It is never the victim’s fault.

name: Disclosure
defs: When a pupil tells an adult about harm. How you listen decides whether they tell anyone again.

name: Guessing program
defs: Software that tries millions of possible passwords, starting with the most common ones and people’s usual tricks.

name: Leak
defs: When a website is hacked and its users’ details, sometimes their passwords, get out. Criminals then try them on other sites.

name: Password manager
defs: An app, often built into your phone or browser, that keeps a different strong password for each account behind one main lock.

name: Warning sign
defs: A clue that a message may be a scam: too good to be true, a hurry, a request for a code or money, an unexpected link, a sender who doesn’t match.

name: Trusted adult
defs: A parent, guardian, teacher or other grown-up you can tell when something online feels wrong.
A grown-up you can ask for help, such as a parent or a teacher.

name: Backup codes
defs: Spare codes you get when you turn on two-step sign-in, to get back in if you lose your phone. Keep them on paper, at home.

name: Hacked account
defs: An account someone else has got into, usually with a stolen or guessed password, and uses as if they were you.

name: Recovery settings
defs: The email address and phone number an app uses to help you get back into your account. Check that they are still yours.

name: Evidence
defs: Screenshots of messages, usernames and payments that show what happened. It helps the bank, the app and the police.

name: Recovery scam
defs: A second scam aimed at people who were already tricked: someone promises to get the money back, for a fee.

name: Active footprint
defs: What you share on purpose, like posts, comments, photos and voice notes.
